skill.name: inbox-placement-monitor
skill.description: Monitor post-send email placement using seed-list results, Gmail Postmaster exports, Microsoft SNDS exports, and ESP deliverability data.
skill.summary: Tracks inbox, spam, promotions, and reputation trends after an email send.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline SEND-S notation, and relative links to documentation. One medium-risk finding is confirmed: SKILL.md line 52 gives a Python helper command that can send live seed emails through Resend when run with --live. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Live seed-send helper can execute a local Python script and initiate outbound email sends.
remediation.suggestion: Keep dry-run as the default, require explicit user confirmation before --live, and reject untrusted sender, recipient, subject, and HTML arguments.

content.value_statement: Post-send email teams need to know where messages landed and why placement changed. This skill turns seed tests, Postmaster data, and SNDS exports into provider-level placement trends.
actual_capabilities: Reads seed-list inbox, spam, and promotions placement by mailbox provider.
Trends Gmail Postmaster domain reputation, IP reputation, spam rate, and feedback-loop signals.
Trends Microsoft SNDS IP status, complaint rate, and spam-trap hits.
Compares a current send against a prior baseline and names each regression.
Produces a SEND-S placement snapshot with Measured, User-provided, or Estimated labels.
limitations: Requires user-provided seed-list, Gmail Postmaster, Microsoft SNDS, or ESP exports.
Does not run SPF, DKIM, or DMARC pre-send checks.
Does not compute the full EQS score or enforce vetoes.
Marks missing provider data as NEEDS_INPUT instead of inferring placement.

use_cases.title: Investigate a Placement Drop
use_cases.description: Compare the latest seed-list test with a prior baseline and name the providers that regressed.

use_cases.title: Trend Sender Reputation
use_cases.description: Review Gmail Postmaster and Microsoft SNDS exports to track reputation direction after each send.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Auditor Snapshot
use_cases.description: Create a SEND-S placement snapshot that another quality gate can use before the next campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Read Latest Send Placement
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this seed-list placement test for [domain]. Show inbox, spam, and promotions placement by provider. Mark missing provider data as NEEDS_INPUT.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Against Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this placement test with my prior send baseline. Name each provider regression, the change in points, and any missing data.

prompt_templates.title: Trend Reputation Signals
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Gmail Postmaster and Microsoft SNDS exports for [domain]. Summarize domain reputation, IP status, complaint rate, and direction.

prompt_templates.title: Build SEND-S Snapshot
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced handoff to a quality gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SEND-S placement snapshot for [domain] using the seed test, Postmaster export, SNDS export, and ESP complaint data. Label each metric source.

output_examples.input: Seed test for example.com shows Gmail 82% inbox, 13% promotions, 5% spam; Outlook 96% inbox; Yahoo missing.
output: Gmail is partially degraded because promotions and spam placement are visible.
Outlook is holding with inbox-dominant placement.
Yahoo is NEEDS_INPUT because the seed test has no Yahoo result.

output_examples.input: Gmail domain reputation moved High to Medium, spam rate rose from 0.08% to 0.14%, and SNDS IP status is yellow.
output: Reputation is degrading across Gmail and Microsoft signals.
The Gmail spam-rate increase crosses the 0.1% red line used by this placement read.
Route the finding to deliverability QA if the next step is an auth or reputation fix.

best_practices: Provide seed-list results and reputation exports from the same send window.
Label manual observations, dashboard exports, and estimates before requesting analysis.
Keep a prior baseline so the skill can report actual send-over-send changes.
anti_patterns: Treating a missing mailbox provider as passing.
Using the skill for pre-send SPF, DKIM, or DMARC checks.
Asking for a full EQS verdict instead of a placement snapshot.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs a seed-list placement result, Gmail Postmaster export, Microsoft SNDS export, ESP deliverability data, or a prior baseline.

faq.question: Can it run without a prior baseline?
faq.answer: Yes. It records the first run as the baseline and avoids inventing a send-over-send delta.

faq.question: Does it check SPF, DKIM, and DMARC?
faq.answer: No. It routes pre-send authentication checks to the deliverability QA skill.

faq.question: Does it compute the full EQS score?
faq.answer: No. It creates a placement snapshot that an email quality auditor can use later.

faq.question: How are missing provider results handled?
faq.answer: Missing providers are marked NEEDS_INPUT. The skill does not pass missing Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, or Apple data by default.

faq.question: Can it send seed emails automatically?
faq.answer: It documents an optional Resend helper. Live sending should require explicit user confirmation and trusted inputs.
